text:
Earwigs -- a beneficial insect group.

Description: recognisable by the pincer-like forceps at the rear of the body, used for defence and prey capture; body length roughly 20-25 mm. Earwigs are nocturnal, hiding in soil or plant debris during the day and becoming active, including on leaves, at night.

Role: earwigs feed on the eggs and larvae of various pest insects and are generally considered a beneficial general predator, though they can occasionally cause minor feeding damage themselves.
